problem: Existing lifelong navigation methods rely on explicit maps or scene graphs, short frame-based memory, or static memories decoupled from policy learning. VLA fine-tuning via RL is episodic and local, so policies cannot accumulate experience or adapt to environment changes over long deployments.
motivation: Lifelong deployment in dynamic real-world spaces needs a persistent, visually grounded memory that keeps improving and directly drives policy learning. Inspired by human visual mental imagery, the paper represents goals as images and co-evolves memory and policy without any human supervision.
key_idea: A self-evolving multimodal memory (keyframes, VLM captions, timestamps) generates self-instructions and image goals, and these drive online conservative-Q-learning RL of an image-goal VLA policy, so scene knowledge is implicitly absorbed into model weights.
insight: Ablations (Table 2) show every component matters: clearing memory each episode drops SR to about 80-86%, replacing self-instruction with random goals gives 87-92% SR and lower SPL, and removing the BC loss gives unstable learning. Swapping in other memories (ReMEmbR) or other RL methods (ConRFT, SERL) also plateaus at 82-94% SR. The gain therefore comes from tightly coupling memory-generated curricula with stable RL, not from either part alone.
method: Pretrained VLA backbone: Qwen2-7B with SigLIP+DINOv2 dual encoders and a 2-layer MLP projector; current frame and goal image at 64 tokens each, history frames pooled by GAP with exponential-decay attention bias (64-frame window); 4-layer MLP head outputs K=8 waypoints (x,y,θ).

Pretraining: imitation (MSE on waypoints) on 50K Habitat HM3D/MP3D trajectories (5M steps, 80% shortest-path expert, 20% random-walk exploration), with heavy sim-to-real augmentation (blur, jitter, noise, camera shake, color blocks, region removal); 14K steps, batch 320.

Self-evolving memory database: keyframes are chosen every 5 steps when cosine embedding change exceeds 0.15; if similarity to the nearest entry is ≤0.7 it is inserted with a Qwen3-VL-8B caption, otherwise the image is replaced only if it aligns better with the stored caption (LLaVE embeddings).
VLM-based retrieval: Qwen3-VL-8B selects the best-matching entry from captions plus timestamps (supports temporal instructions) and returns a confidence score.

Self-instruction and hybrid goal retrieval: every 10 episodes or +20% memory growth, the VLM generates 50 instructions (object, functional, spatial, compositional, temporal); goals come from memory, with fallback to internet images if confidence <0.6 or with probability max(0,1-|M|/20).
Reward: LLaVE cosine similarity between current view and goal; +10 on stop with sim≥0.75, +2 for first crossing of 0.5/0.6/0.7, -0.01 per step, -0.1 per collision.
CQL online optimization: MLP critic with CQL regularizer (α=5, γ=0.99) and actor loss -Q plus BC on successful transitions (λ=0.1), run in a parallel process with updates every 100 steps.

setting.backbone: Qwen2-7B VLA (SigLIP+DINOv2, pretrained then RL-fine-tuned online); Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct frozen for captioning/retrieval/instruction generation; LLaVE-7B frozen for embeddings and reward
setting.training_data: 50K Habitat trajectories (5M steps) on HM3D/MP3D train scenes for pretraining; internet indoor image collection for fallback goals; then online self-generated RL in the target scene with no labels
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (120° FOV on real robot) plus goal image and RGB history; no depth/odometry in policy
setting.action_space: continuous waypoint sequence (8 waypoints, x/y/heading) in the robot frame, executed by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: none at test time (reward from LLaVE similarity; retrieval accuracy human-checked only for analysis)

Sim results are per-scene on 5 unseen scenes with a custom protocol (no standard benchmark); Len is episode length in steps. Table 1 has no aggregated average, so all 5 scenes are listed. Dynamic/large-scene/ambiguous-instruction results (final-stage online EMA SR 96.4/74.7/83.8) are in Table 4 and not repeated above.
results: On five unseen Habitat scenes AllDayNav reaches 96-99% SR, SPL 56.4-58.8 and the shortest episodes (97-109 steps). It beats ReMEmbR, ConRFT, SERL (SR up to 94%, SPL ≤54.4) and the OSG Navigator scene-graph baseline (SR 75-77%). On a real Unitree Go2 it improves from 49-60% eval SR at initialization to 87-97% in three environments, and recovers after abrupt scene changes.
limitations: Depends on large VLMs (Qwen3-VL-8B, LLaVE-7B) and heavy compute (8 H100 online, remote server over 5G), with ~5 Hz speed.
Exploration is not safety-constrained; ambiguous instructions and very large scenes converge slowly (large scene SR only ~75%).

Evaluation is on a custom protocol with reward-model-judged success, 5 sim scenes and 3 real spaces, and no standard benchmarks; the paper does not explain how baselines ConRFT/SERL/ReMEmbR were reproduced in the same framework.
